papers.title: Can LLMs Take Psychological Surveys? A Case Study Using DeepSeek Models on Studies of Jealousy and Consent.
papers.abstract: Online platforms such as Amazon's MTurk enable researchers to collect large amounts of data quickly and efficiently, but the potential presence of bots threatens the validity of such data. These concerns have been mitigated to some extent by the ease of detecting bot-produced data. The present study tested whether data generated by DeepSeek, a large language model (LLM), might prove less detectable by (1) avoiding tell-tale signs characteristic of data produced by unsophisticated bots, and (2) producing results that mirror results from human samples. We tested this in two sexuality-related research contexts. First, we examined whether DeepSeek was able to replicate the sex difference in jealousy (Buss et al., 1992). Second, we examined whether DeepSeek rated safewords as more important for pick-up play than for BDSM scenes conducted between romantic relationship partners (Tarleton et al., 2025). We tested DeepSeek's performance with four models, each with increasing parameter count, corresponding to sophistication and computational cost to use. For the sex difference in jealousy, the highest-level model produced a significant, theory-consistent sex difference but lower-level models failed to do so. For safewords, one of the four models replicated the effect observed in humans, with the highest-level model producing homogeneous results in which nearly all "participants" indicated that safewords were extremely important in both contexts and lower-level models producing noisier results with no difference between contexts. In addition, DeepSeek had particular difficulty reflecting assigned demographics on questions with select-all-that-apply formats, sometimes selecting all options in a manner that would be implausible in human respondents. papers.title: [Psychotrichological disorders-hair and the psyche in the biopsychosocial context].
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychotrichological disorders play an important role in dermatological practice. The biopsychosocial model provides a fundamental framework for understanding the causal, triggering, and accompanying psychological factors associated with hair and hair loss disorders. OBJECTIVE: Psychological symptoms and comorbidities are common among patients with hair disorders, particularly hair loss disorders, and represent a significant challenge in clinical practice. Understanding the close relationship between psychological factors and hair disorders provides the basis for a biopsychosocial management approach that considers biological, psychological, and social factors. METHODS: An overview of common psychotrichological disorders, key psychological symptoms and comorbidities, and biopsychosocial management strategies is provided. RESULTS: Hair and hair loss disorders highlight the close bidirectional relationship between the hair and scalp and psychological health. Psychological comorbidities, psychosocial burden, and impaired quality of life are common among patients with hair and hair loss disorders, and should therefore be identified early, systematically assessed, and treated as clinically indicated. Psychotrichological disorders can broadly be classified into primary mental disorders affecting the hair and hair growth and primary hair disorders with secondary effects on mental health. CONCLUSION: A biopsychosocial and interdisciplinary treatment approach forms the basis of patient-centered care. Early assessment of psychological distress and its integration into diagnosis and treatment may contribute to improved treatment outcomes, coping with the condition, and quality of life. papers.title: CH5 benzothiazole schiff base protects against DEHP-induced testicular injury via involvement of COX-2-associated inflammatory signaling and spermatogenesis recovery in adult zebrafish.
papers.abstract: The reproductive system is impacted by the endocrine disrupting chemical di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) as a result of oxidative stress, inflammation, and disruption of steroidogenesis. The objective of the current investigation was to assess the therapeutic efficacy of a benzothiazole-based schiff base CH5 derivative in the treatment of DEHP-induced testicular injury. Adult male zebrafish were exposed to DEHP (20 μg/L) treatment for 21 days to cause testicular damage, after which CH5 (50 μM and 75 μM) and clomiphene citrate (positive control) were administered orally for 14 days. The protective effect of CH5 was evaluated using in silico, in vitro, behavioral, sperm quality, reproductive health, biochemical, and mRNA expression. In silico analysis identified the key target proteins, such as esr1, cox-2, egfr, hsp90, and igf1r, while molecular docking has indicated that cox-2 possesses the highest binding affinity to CH5. Also, the derivative exhibited low cytotoxicity, potent antioxidant activity, and minimal embryotoxicity at therapeutic concentrations up to 75 μM. Therapeutic treatment with CH5 (75 μM) significantly improved courtship and mate recognition behavior by increasing female interactions, improving sperm concentration (6.63 × 10⁶ sperm/mL), reducing intracellular ROS in sperm cells, enhancing fertilization and hatching rates. In addition, the activities of SOD, CAT, and GST were enhanced by CH5, while LDH and MPO were diminished. Also, CH5 treatment improves the gonadosomatic index (3.56%), preserved testicular structure, upregulated esr1 expression and downregulated il-1β, tnf-α, inos and cox-2. These results indicate that CH5 demonstrates its prospective promise as a therapeutic candidate against endocrine disruptor-induced male reproductive toxicity.

papers.title: Small poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma with concentric periarterial growth causing popliteal arterial stenosis: a case report.
papers.abstract: Soft-tissue sarcomas arising in the popliteal fossa are uncommon but clinically important because of their close relationship to major neurovascular structures. Poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma is an aggressive histologic subtype of synovial sarcoma. We report a case of a small poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma located in the perivascular region of the popliteal fossa that showed concentric periarterial growth with popliteal arterial stenosis. A 68-year-old woman reported a several-month history of heaviness in the right lower extremity. Ultrasonography revealed a 2-cm irregular hypoechoic solid mass circumferentially surrounding the popliteal artery, with no definite internal Doppler flow. The lesion showed intermediate signal intensity on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous intermediate-to-high signal intensity on fat-suppressed T2-weighted images. MRI showed circumferential arterial encasement with stenosis. Non-contrast-enhanced quiescent-interval slice-selective (QISS) MRA helped define the longitudinal extent of popliteal arterial narrowing. Surgical resection required vascular resection and reconstruction bypass of the popliteal artery and vein. Histopathological examination showed nested proliferation of tumor cells with ovoid-to-round nuclei in a hyalinized fibrous stroma. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for SS18-SSX and SSX, supporting the diagnosis of synovial sarcoma. This case illustrates that even a small synovial sarcoma in the popliteal fossa can circumferentially encase the popliteal artery and cause stenosis.

papers.title: The paracondylar process: anatomical relationships and clinical implications.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: The paracondylar process (PCP) is a rare and infrequently reported anatomical variant, where the incomplete separation of the lowest occipital sclerotome (proatlas) and uppermost cervical sclerotome results in a complete bony projection that meets with an epitransverse process of the atlas. We report a case that highlights the imaging and anatomical relationships of the PCP, particularly with the vertebral artery (VA), which has been given little attention in literature despite its important symptomatic and neurosurgical implications. CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old male presented with longstanding limitation to neck movement, left‑sided headaches and occasional dizzy spells. Cervical computed tomography (CT) imaging demonstrated a bony strut projecting inferiorly from the skull base, laterally adjacent to the left occipital condyle, articulating with the epitransverse process of C1. Though CT angiography was not performed, close examination of the course of the left vertebral artery on the soft tissue CT windows demonstrated an intimate relationship of the artery coursing immediately medial to the bony process in its V3 segment. We present a three-dimensional reconstruction prepared via segmentation and close reading of the soft tissue CT to illuminate the expected course of the vertebral artery and its' relationship to the PCP. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates the anatomical and clinical significance of the paracondylar process (PCP), with a particular focus on its relationship with the vertebral artery. Whilst rare, this finding carries important clinical implications if surgical resection is to be contemplated.

papers.title: Bismuth-Sulfur Engineered Zero-Valent Iron Prioritizes Chloramphenicol-Class Antibiotics Dechlorination Over Hydrogen Evolution and Nitro Reduction.
papers.abstract: Chloramphenicol (CAP) and florfenicol (FF), as chloramphenicol-class antibiotics, often coexist in wastewater, where chlorine substituents largely determine their toxicity. Although zero-valent iron (ZVI) is a promising reductive remediation material, its poor chemoselectivity and preferential electron consumption by hydrogen evolution (HER) and nitro-reduction severely limit the detoxification of chlorinated moieties. Herein, we develop bismuth-sulfur co-intercalated ZVI (Bi-S-ZVI) to reduce CAP+FF co-contaminants, achieving enhanced nitro-reduction (22-74-fold), dechlorination (175-419-fold), and low HER. Notably, the dechlorination selectivity (defined as the ratio of FF dechlorination to CAP nitro-reduction) increased from 0.3%-2% to 39%, and Bi-S-ZVI enabled a distinct pathway where dechlorination preceded nitro-reduction in the -NO2/-Cl co-substituted CAP molecule. Mechanistically, Bi2S3 and Bi0 are the dominant contributors to the reactivity and dechlorination selectivity of Bi-S-ZVI, respectively. Bi2S3 couples galvanically with Fe0 to generate a built-in electric field and creates Fe-S-Bi charge-transfer channels to accelerate electron transport. Bi0 selectively associates with ─Cl as a halogen-bond acceptor. Bi2S3 and Bi0 synergistically suppress HER by increasing surface hydrophobicity and hindering atomic hydrogen recombination, while Bi2S3 further disrupts the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network. This work provides a cost-effective and scalable strategy for selective reductive remediation, overcoming the reactivity-selectivity-stability trade-offs of existing iron materials.

papers.title: Burden of informal caregiving for stroke survivors in the Philippines: a cross-sectional survey of sociodemographic and caregiving factors.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Stroke imposes significant burden on informal caregivers (ICs) in the Philippines, yet factors associated with caregiver strain remain unclear. This study examined sociodemographic and caregiving factors associated with burden among stroke ICs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional survey of 462 Filipino ICs collected sociodemographic characteristics, caregiver responsibilities and strain using the Modified Caregiver Strain Index-Filipino (MCSI-F). Data were analyzed using chi-square tests and ordinal logistic regression. RESULTS: Caregivers were predominantly female (75.3%), spouses/partners (47.8%), and economically disadvantaged (66.9%). Median MCSI-F score was 22 (IQR = 8), indicating no burden, while 11.9% reported severe strain. In the multivariable ordinal logistic regression model, work interference showed the strongest adjusted association with higher burden severity (aOR = 5.38, p < 0.001), followed by spousal relationship (aOR = 2.10, p = 0.028); male sex was protective (aOR = 0.34, p < 0.001), and providing <1 h/day of care (vs. >6 h/day) was associated with lower burden (aOR = 0.17, p = 0.004). Age, income, employment status, education, religion, and urban-rural residence were not significant after adjustment. Parallel lines held (p = 0.765), and Nagelkerke's R2 was 0.231. CONCLUSIONS: Filipino stroke ICs experience substantial strain primarily driven by work interference and intensive caregiving hours, with spouses and female caregivers disproportionately affected.
